ai.title: Retry web search credits charge up to 3 times
ai.summary: The web search API endpoint in `web/src/app/api/v1/web-search/_post.ts` now retries the `checkCreditsAndCharge` call up to 3 times if it fails. This addresses flaky credit charging failures by introducing a loop with exponential backoff (`sleep(1000 * attempt)`). The change is scoped to the backend API logic, specifically the `postWebSearch` function. If all retries fail, the original error response is returned; if successful, the `creditsUsed` value is extracted from the final successful attempt.

eli5.text: When someone does a web search, the system tries to charge their account for that search. If that charge doesn't go through the first time, it now tries again up to two more times instead of immediately giving up. You would notice this if you saw a web search fail in the past for a mysterious payment-related reason: the system would retry the charge internally before showing you an error, so those flaky failures become less frequent.

ai.title: Add global error handlers in web server
ai.summary: Added `web/instrumentation.ts` to register global `unhandledRejection` and `uncaughtException` handlers. Prevents Node.js process crashes from unhandled errors, avoiding 502 Bad Gateway responses from Render's proxy. Logs critical errors via `logger` but does not exit the process, allowing continued request handling.

eli5.text: When the web server starts up, it now quietly catches any unexpected errors that happen in the background instead of letting them crash the whole server. This means visitors are less likely to see a '502 Bad Gateway' error message when something goes wrong during a request. The server logs these serious mistakes for the team to review later, but keeps running so other visitors can still use the site. This fix is live today and applies to anyone using the web application.

ai.title: Add retry logic to SDK agent runtime client fetches
ai.summary: Added `fetchWithRetry` to `sdk/src/impl/database.ts` and retry loops to `packages/agent-runtime/src/llm-api/codebuff-web-api.ts`. Both now handle transient HTTP errors (408, 429, 5xx) and network failures with exponential backoff. `database.ts` uses shared `MAX_RETRIES_PER_MESSAGE` and `RETRY_BACKOFF_BASE_DELAY_MS` from `retry-config`, while `codebuff-web-api.ts` defines local constants (`MAX_RETRIES = 3`, `RETRY_BASE_DELAY_MS = 1000`) and caps at 3 attempts. Scope covers SDK database calls and agent-runtime web API requests.

eli5.text: When the assistant tries to talk to the company's servers to get an answer, it sometimes hits a temporary problem like a busy signal or slow connection. Now, instead of giving up right away, it automatically tries again a few times with short pauses in between, so you're less likely to see an error message when the service is just briefly overloaded.

ai.title: Rename /chats to /history in CLI command registry
ai.summary: Primary slash command renamed from /chats to /history. Old /chats name retained as alias. Scope limited to command-registry.ts and slash-commands.ts. Alias ensures backward compatibility for existing muscle memory.

eli5.text: The command you type to look at your past conversations has been renamed from /chats to /history, while /chats still works as a shortcut so existing habits aren't broken. This only affects people typing these commands in the CLI tool, which is already live today.

ai.title: CLI login modal shows fallback URL
ai.summary: The CLI login modal now displays the raw `loginUrl` as a fallback option. This change addresses devices where the automatic browser opening via `open()` fails. Implemented in `cli/src/components/login-modal.tsx`, the UI updates the primary prompt to 'Opening browser...' and adds a secondary section labeled 'Or copy this URL if browser didn't open:' containing the exact link.

eli5.text: When you sign in on a device where the program cannot automatically open your web browser, the login screen now shows the web address you need and tells you to copy and paste it yourself. Instead of just saying to click a link, it lets you complete sign-in by manually opening that address in your browser.

ai.title: Fix STEPTEXT agent streaming in CLI
ai.summary: STEP_TEXT agents now stream assistant text directly via onResponseChunk in run-programmatic-step.ts, replacing the previous logic that overwrote streamed content with final result extraction in sdk-event-handlers.ts. This ensures agents like commander preserve their live output instead of displaying a static final message. The change affects CLI event handling and the agent runtime's programmatic step execution.

eli5.text: When you run a STEP_TEXT agent in the command-line tool, its live typed output now appears as it happens instead of being replaced by a single final message at the end. The older logic that swapped in the final result is gone; the agent's streamed text is preserved in real time, so you see progress as it happens. This is live today in the CLI.

ai.title: Fix CLI integration tests for retry logic
ai.summary: Updated `api-integration.test.ts` to mock `@codebuff/common/testing/mock-modules` and zero out retry delays via `retry-config`. Tests now expect multiple fetch calls due to `fetchWithRetry` behavior on network errors, replacing previous single-call assertions. Cleanup added in `afterEach` via `clearMockedModules`.

eli5.text: The automated tests that check whether the command-line tool retries failed network connections have been corrected so they now match how the tool actually behaves. If you ran these tests before, they would have passed even though the real tool keeps trying after a dropped connection; now the tests expect that repeated-attempt behavior. This only affects the internal quality checks developers run and is already live in the test suite, with no impact on what you see when using the command-line tool yourself.

ai.title: CLI API integration tests mock setTimeout for speed
ai.summary: API integration tests now mock globalThis.setTimeout directly instead of using mockModule on retry-config. This avoids async module mocking overhead and ensures retry delays execute instantly. Scoped to cli/src/__tests__/integration/api-integration.test.ts. Original setTimeout is stored and restored in afterEach to prevent leakage.

eli5.text: If you ran the automated checks that make sure the assistant talks to the server correctly, they now finish faster instead of pausing on purpose to wait between retry attempts. The checks still do exactly the same thing they always did, they just no longer sit idle during built-in delays before trying again. You won't see anything different unless you're running those checks yourself, but when you do, the tests that used to take a little longer will now run through the waiting parts instantly. The system saves the real timer before each check and puts it back afterward, so no other part of the program is affected.

ai.title: Replace as-any casts with typed error helpers
ai.summary: Type safety improved by replacing `as any` casts with typed error helpers and `instanceof Error` checks. New `common/src/testing/errors.ts` provides `createNodeError` and `createPostgresError` for structured test mocks. CLI `publish.ts` and Web profile components (`api-keys`, `referrals`, `security`) updated to use explicit types instead of unchecked casts. This eliminates silent type errors in error handling paths across core and UI layers.

eli5.text: The app now shows error messages the honest way instead of guessing at them. When something fails behind the scenes, it checks first whether the failure is actually an error message before deciding what to display, rather than treating every unknown thing as if it carried a message it might not have. For you as someone using the publish command or the profile sections like API keys, referrals, or security settings, this means the messages you see when something goes wrong are more reliable and less likely to disappear into confusing empty text. This improvement is already live.

ai.title: Block sensitive files with strikethrough UI
ai.summary: A new FileFilter in createRunConfig blocks sensitive files (.env, .pem, id_rsa, credentials, etc.) and tags .env.example/.env.sample/.env.template as example-only; getFiles applies that filter, returns FILE_READ_STATUS.IGNORED for blocked files and prepends FILE_READ_STATUS.TEMPLATE to example content. The CLI read_files component renders blocked paths in strikethrough with '(blocked)' and example paths with '(allowed - example only)'. FILE_READ_STATUS.IGNORED is renamed to '[BLOCKED]' and a TEMPLATE status is added to common/src/old-constants.ts, and the SDK now exports getFiles plus the FileFilter and FileFilterResult types.
ai.evidence: cli/src/utils/create-run-config.ts defines isSensitiveFile (matching SENSITIVE_EXTENSIONS, SENSITIVE_BASENAMES, SENSITIVE_PATTERNS) and isEnvTemplateFile (ENV_TEMPLATE_SUFFIXES), and createRunConfig wires a FileFilter returning {status:'blocked'} / {status:'allow-example'} that sdk/src/tools/read-files.ts getFiles consumes, prepending FILE_READ_STATUS.TEMPLATE to example files. cli/src/components/tools/read-files.tsx now renders sensitive files with strikethrough and '(blocked)' via FilePathsDescription, while sdk/src/index.ts exports getFiles, FileFilter, and FileFilterResult. common/src/old-constants.ts renames FILE_READ_STATUS.IGNORED to '[BLOCKED]' and adds TEMPLATE: '[TEMPLATE]'.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show consumers outside the CLI and SDK read_files path for the new FileFilter, nor whether blocking is enforced server-side or only on the client.

changes.what: read_files tool renders sensitive files in strikethrough with '(blocked)' and env templates with '(allowed - example only)' via FilePathsDescription in read-files.tsx, backed by isSensitiveFile and isEnvTemplateFile from create-run-config.

getFiles applies an optional FileFilter, returning IGNORED for blocked files and prepending the TEMPLATE marker to example files; run.ts threads fileFilter through requestFiles and requestOptionalFile.
FILE_READ_STATUS.IGNORED renamed to '[BLOCKED]' and a new TEMPLATE: '[TEMPLATE]' status added to old-constants.
getFiles, FileFilter, and FileFilterResult exported from sdk/src/index.ts.

ai.title: Add File Filtering API reference to SDK README
ai.summary: Added `fileFilter` API documentation to `sdk/README.md`. Explains `CodebuffClient` usage with `blocked`, `allow-example`, and `allow` statuses. Clarifies default gitignore behavior versus custom filter ownership.

eli5.text: The built-in guide that explains how your assistant-friendly tool can hide or reveal specific files now includes a clearer section on how file filtering works. If you peek at that guide today, you can read plain-language examples showing how returning one of three statuses, blocked, allow-example, or allow, directly controls whether the tool blocks a file, treats it as a template, or reads it normally, including a note that handing the tool its own custom filter list means you take full responsibility for deciding what stays hidden versus what gets read.

ai.title: Remove duplicated .agents build artifacts from SDK package
ai.summary: Deleted `sdk/.agents/constants.js` and type definition files (`agent-definition.js`, `secret-agent-definition.js`, `tools.js`, `util-types.js`) which were accidentally included in the SDK distribution. These files contained compiled JavaScript and source maps for internal agent logic, causing package bloat and potential import conflicts. The cleanup ensures the SDK only ships necessary public interfaces and runtime code.

eli5.text: If you downloaded the software toolkit for adding AI features to your own apps, you may have noticed it was larger than necessary because it accidentally bundled some internal helper files alongside the real tools. The toolkit maintainer removed five duplicate copies of those internal helpers from the published package, so future downloads are smaller and won't include confusing extra files that shouldn't have been there. This is already live, and the only thing you'd notice is a slightly smaller download and no more stray files showing up if you peek inside the toolkit's contents.

ai.title: CLI version bumped to 1.0.581
ai.summary: The Codebuff CLI package manifest at `cli/release/package.json` was updated to reflect version `1.0.581`, advancing from `1.0.580` as part of the day's release cycle. This version bump encapsulates prior commits introducing web search retry logic, global error handlers in the web server, SDK agent runtime retry mechanisms, CLI command registry aliasing, login modal fallback URLs, STEPTEXT agent streaming fixes, test improvements, type safety enhancements, and sensitive file filtering. The change originates from the `cli/` package, which manages CLI binary distribution and release packaging within the Freebuff monorepo architecture.
ai.evidence: The commit `ee7b669c` modifies `cli/release/package.json`, incrementing the `version` field from `1.0.580` to `1.0.581` within the Codebuff CLI package manifest. No other files were changed in this commit, which aligns with its classification as a release-bump operation.

eli5.text: This release makes the CLI more stable and user-friendly by fixing crashes, improving error handling, and protecting sensitive files. Web search credit charging now retries automatically up to three times when it fails temporarily, reducing interruptions during online searches. The login process now shows a fallback URL so users can manually open their browser when the automatic prompt fails on some devices. Agent output now streams live instead of showing only the final message, making interactive sessions smoother and more responsive. Sensitive files like private keys and.env files are now blocked from being read, while example files like.env.example remain accessible. Upgrading gives you better reliability during searches, easier sign-in on tricky devices, live streaming from agents, and stronger protection against accidentally exposing secrets.

ai.summary: New `Clickable` component in `cli/src/components/clickable.tsx` wraps interactive regions to automatically disable text selection, preventing accidental highlighting during clicks. `CopyButton` refactored into `copy-button.tsx` using this new primitive, replacing the previous `copy-icon-button.tsx` implementation and its associated hook. eli5.text: When you click buttons and other interactive elements in the command-line interface, the text inside them no longer gets accidentally highlighted. The system now consistently prevents text selection across all clickable areas, so tapping a button won't leave stray highlighted text behind. This affects everyone using the CLI today.
